title: Kibbeh
description: Kibbeh is a traditional Levantine Arabic dish made from a mixture of fine bulgur wheat and minced meat, shaped into stuffed croquettes and either fried or baked. It features a spiced meat filling and a crisp golden exterior with a soft, flavorful interior.

ingredients.title: For the Shell (Kibbeh Dough)
items: Cold water as needed (about ½ cup)

ingredients.title: For the Filling
items: 300g ground beef or lamb (preferably with some fat)
2 tbsp olive oil or clarified butter

instruction.title: Instructions
steps:
1. Prepare the Bulgur:
• Rinse and soak bulgur in cold water for 30 minutes.
• Drain and squeeze out excess moisture.
• Mix with ground meat, grated onion, and spices.
• Knead for 10 minutes until a smooth dough forms.

2. Prepare the Filling:
• Heat oil in a pan.
• Sauté onions until soft.
• Add ground meat and cook until browned.
• Stir in pine nuts, spices, salt, and pepper.
• Cook until mixture is dry, then cool.

3. Shape the Kibbeh:
Fried version:
• Form dough into balls and hollow out centers.
• Fill with meat mixture and seal into oval shapes.

Baked version:
• Press half dough into tray.
• Add filling layer.
• Cover with remaining dough and score.

4. Cook:
Frying:
• Fry at 180°C (350°F) for 5–7 minutes until golden.

Baking:
• Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 30–35 minutes until crisp and golden.

5. Serve:
• Serve warm with yogurt, tahini, or Arabic salad.
• Garnish with pine nuts and sumac.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve with garlic yogurt or tahini sauce
Pair with fresh Arabic salad or tabouleh
Enjoy as an appetizer or main dish
Garnish with toasted pine nuts and sumac

chefTips: Use very finely ground meat for a smooth kibbeh shell.
Fine bulgur is essential for proper texture and elasticity.
Ensure filling is dry to prevent bursting during frying.
Maintain steady oil temperature for even frying.
Chilling shaped kibbeh before frying helps them hold shape better.
